title: Niho Scotish Garden Residents Welfare Association v. U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Manjive Shukla, JJ.
disposition: Writ dismissed for want of prosecution; Clause 7.10 view only prima facie.
headnote: On 3 January 2018 Tarun Agarwala and Saumitra Dayal Singh, JJ. recorded a prima facie view that the controversy could not be considered by the Ombudsman under Clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and called for a counter affidavit. The writ was later dismissed for want of prosecution on 17 March 2023 when none appeared to press it; any interim order stood discharged. The Clause 7.10 point was never finally decided.
facts: Niho Scotish Garden Residents Welfare Association petitioned the Allahabad High Court against the U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission and three others. On 3 January 2018 a Division Bench recorded a prima facie view that the controversy could not be considered by the Ombudsman under Clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, directed respondents 1 and 2 to file a counter affidavit, and issued notice to respondent 4. After an adjournment in January 2023, none appeared on 17 March 2023.

holding_units.holding: Prima facie, the controversy could not be considered by the Ombudsman under Clause 7.10 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The writ was later dismissed for want of prosecution without a merits ruling; any interim order stood discharged.

not_decided.point: Whether the controversy was outside the Ombudsman's Clause 7.10 jurisdiction
not_decided.note: The 3 January 2018 observation was only prima facie; the writ was dismissed for want of prosecution without deciding that question or the underlying dispute.
